text:
Looking ahead to the 2050s under a high emissions scenario, the best match for the field is Walla Walla County, WA. Six of the eight climate models agree on this good match. A lower sigma means the place's climate today is closer to the farm's future climate.

Out of the matching areas checked, two use the field's current rotation, which is a flexible mix of pulses, spring wheat, and winter wheat. Other rotations used at the matching places include winter wheat transitioning to fallow, a flexible mix of fallow, pulses, and winter wheat, and a flexible mix of fallow, spring wheat, and winter wheat.

Comparing hazards with the best match, the field has 27 days above 32c per year today compared to 37 at the match. The field has 172 frost-free days compared to 211 at the match. For afternoon ground temperature, June is 30.5c at the field and 35.7c at the match, while July-August is 42.1c at the field and 46.5c at the match. Driest-month soil water in September is 18.1 percent at the field and 17.8 percent at the match.

Overall, the climate models project warming across all parts of the year, with varying changes in precipitation.

Candidates are drawn from 3351 farmland cells.
